correctness.rationale: For any clique anchor, the cited exact Type-A criterion gives a unique alternating interval for every neighbor. Comparing toggles yields just two possibilities for an adjacent pair of such neighbors: nested endpoint-sharing intervals whose other endpoints differ by at least two, or disjoint consecutive intervals with a matched two-symbol pair and an equal source-symbol join. A family without disjoint intervals has one common endpoint by the pairwise-intersecting-edge property in a bipartite graph. A family with a disjoint pair is forced into two pencils with one common boundary. Both families have at most floor(n/2) intervals. A direct prefix-toggle construction on an alternating word reaches the upper bound. The accompanying checker tests independent descendant-ball adjacency and maximal-clique structure for the exact listed finite ranges; these checks supplement rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: The exact q-independent clique number is a natural obstruction in two-read deletion reconstruction, and the complete anchored one/two-pencil classification is a stronger structural result than a modest numerical improvement. It identifies every possible high-order mutually confusable family and supplies constraints that can inform clique-based reconstruction bounds; it does not claim to settle code capacity or independent-set size.
